notes: Covers the L7, L8 and L9 in Home, LTD and Club versions. Home units use a PWM motor control board, while LTD and Club units use an SCR board (P/N 70080 for 110 V or 70081 for 220 V).

gaps: No horsepower for the drive motor and no part number for the home PWM board or relay board were found in the text.
The parts list gives 70222 both for the L8/L9 drive belt and for the 110 V motor brush; p. 60 confirms 70222 as the 90 VDC brush.
No production years are claimed (the Sport Trainer console is listed as 1999-present).
method: Source: Landice L-Series Home & Commercial Treadmill Diagnostic & Service Manual, 2003, Version C/D.2 (Internet Archive copy, 127 pages, read as text on 2026-11-12; PDF page numbers match the printed ones).

Part numbers used here are the ones the parts list (pp. 31-34) marks L7 or L7/L8/L9; elevation motor and potentiometer numbers are repeated on p. 74, SCR board, display board and fuse numbers come from the L7/L8/L9 flow charts (pp. 100, 105).
The SCR board needs an external capacitor and filter choke.
The 220 V figures (180 VDC motor, 70125, 70126) apply to 220 V Club units only.
Qty 1 on extra parts is inferred from single listings.

comps.spec: Drive motor P/N 70014 (110 V units; 70125 on 220 V units), brushed DC. Landice says 110 VAC treadmills use a 90 VDC drive motor (220 VAC units a 180 VDC one) and that, spun by hand, the 90 VDC motor gives roughly 10 VDC per mph. Brushes P/N 70222 (90 VDC), replace below 3/8 in.

Home units: PWM motor control board, line AC in on L1/L2, DC out to the motor on A+/A- (90 VDC from a 120 VAC unit), speed reference on V+/P1/P2 (0-7 VDC), MAX, MIN and IR trim pots, no external capacitor or choke needed. LTD/Club units: SCR board P/N 70080 (110 V) or 70081 (220 V) instead

Relay board (only on units with the PWM board): belt (motor start) relay and elevation UP and DOWN relays that switch line voltage to the elevation motor; also controls the DC transformer that powers the upper display, and carries diagnostic LEDs

Fuse on the AC input of the relay board (home) or SCR board (LTD/Club): MDA-20, named as the slow-blow fuse on 110 V SCR boards and as the spare for the relay board fuse; 110 V units fuse only the hot leg, 220 V units have two fuses; a spare fuse is drawn in the PWM motor pan
12 VDC power supply (transformer type) feeding the upper display board on PWM (home) units; 12.0 to 17.0 VDC output counts as good

Elevation motor P/N 70088 (110 V; 70126 on 220 V units), runs on 120/220 VAC switched by the relay board (home) or SCR board (LTD/Club), turns a 3/4 in. elevation screw and nut, has a lower limit switch
Elevation potentiometer P/N 71013 fitted to the elevation motor, 0-1000 ohm track (brown, orange and blue wires), reports incline position to the upper display
Magnetic speed sensor P/N 71007 on bracket 70067, reads the drive motor flywheel at about 1/16 in. gap
L7 drive belt 220J10 (L8/L9 use 70222), flywheel 70010 on the drive motor, L7 drive roller sheave CV-18-2 pressed onto the front roller
L7 drive roller 70236 (front) and take-up roller 70237 (rear)
Both rollers turn on bearings at each end; parts list (L7/L8/L9) gives bearing block P/N 70373 (wide, single piece) or 70034 (two pieces) and wide bearing block spacer 70403
Upper display board, P/N by console: 70252 Executive Trainer, 70308 Cardio Trainer, 70281 Pro Trainer, 70329 Sport Trainer, 70424 Pro Sports Trainer
